text.p: Investment bank Okasan International E.C. said on Monday it liquidated its Bahrain office from July 1, as forecast earlier this year.
"Shareholders of Okasan International have decided at an extraordinary meeting to voluntarily liquidate the company from July 1," a bank official told Reuters.
"The secondary market has not been good in the past seven years, prompting the closure of the bank," the official said. "The company is not existing any more (in Bahrain)," he added.
Ernst & Young has been appointed liquidator for the Bahrain-based bank.
Bank officials said in May the bank would officially be closed on June 30 and had cleared the way for the closure with the Bahraini authorities.
Bankers said Okasan is 51 percent owned by Okasan Securities of Japan. Financial institutions in Bahrain and Kuwait and Marubeni International Finance Plc held the remaining stake.
